title: Host Support Academy: Cancellation-Rate Restrictions on Host Accounts
content:
# Host Support Academy — Restrictions on Host Accounts

## The rule in one paragraph

After every host cancellation, the cancellation rate of the Host Accounts holder is evaluated once the account has at least the tier's minimum number of stays in the lookback. A rate at or above the tier's cancellation-rate threshold restricts the account for the tier's restriction period of calendar days, and the last day of the restriction is the restriction date plus that many days, less one. During the restriction the account's listings accept no new bookings, while confirmed stays continue. Reaching the tier's restriction strike count in the strike lookback also restricts the account for the same period. A restriction is lifted only after the restricted-until date has passed: the restriction ends at the end of the restricted-until date, so it may be lifted from the following calendar day (1 day after it), unless an account restriction appeal is approved earlier, in which case it is lifted on approval.

## Questions and answers

**What is the cancellation rate?** It is 100 times the number of host cancellations of the account dated in the lookback window that were initiated by the host and whose penalty was not waived, divided by the number of the account's stays whose check-in date falls in the window (in any status other than requested, declined or expired) plus those host cancellations, rounded half up to 2 decimal places. The window is the tier's lookback of calendar days ending on the day of the evaluation.

**Hypothetical figure:** 2 such cancellations and 38 such stays give 100 times 2, divided by 40, which is 5.00%.

**When is the rate applied at all?** Only once the account has at least the tier's minimum number of stays in the lookback.

**What does "at or above" mean at the threshold?** A rate equal to the tier's threshold restricts the account.

**How long is the restriction?** For a 30-day restriction period imposed on 10 May, the restricted-until date is 8 June (10 May plus 30 days, less one).

**From when may the restriction be lifted?** It ends at the end of 8 June; it may be lifted from 9 June. On 8 June it is not yet lifted on the strength of the date.

| Date of the lift (hypothetical restricted-until date 8 June) | Account restriction appeal approved earlier? | Lifted? |
|---|---|---|
| 8 June | No | No — the restricted-until date has not passed |
| 9 June | No | Yes |
| 20 May | Yes, approved 20 May | Yes — lifted on approval |

**Do confirmed stays survive the restriction?** Yes. Only new bookings are blocked.
